companyDescription: Sidewalk delivery robots · Uber Eats/DoorDash-partnered autonomous delivery fleet (Uber spinout), scaling fast (fleet nearing 2,000 units, revenue +578% YoY in Q1 2026) with heavy cash burn and a 29% short interest that has repeatedly fueled squeeze moves
priceNote: Rallying into the Aug 6 print after a rough July (-19.5% over 10 days on dilution/funding concerns); still down ~16% YTD 2026
summary: Serve Robotics reports Q2 2026 earnings Aug 6 with revenue growing explosively off a small base (Q1 2026 revenue +578% YoY, +238% sequential) as its Uber Eats/DoorDash-partnered delivery-robot fleet scales toward 2,000 units. With 29% short interest, this stock has repeatedly delivered outsized moves on earnings — Q4 2025 results triggered an ~11% pre-market pop that extended another ~10% intraday on short-squeeze dynamics — but it has also sold off hard on funding/dilution concerns (-19.5% over 10 days in late July 2026). Cash runway is adequate (~$197M liquidity as of Q1 2026 vs -$117.6M levered FCF TTM, so more than 12 months at the current burn rate) but not comfortable, and the unit economics of robot delivery at scale remain genuinely unproven.

catalysts.name: Q2 2026 earnings — Aug 6
catalysts.description: Revenue growth expected to continue off Q1's 578% YoY pace; watch for 2026 guidance ($26M) reaffirmation and cash-burn commentary. 29% short interest raises squeeze potential on a beat.

risks: High cash burn (-$117.6M levered FCF TTM) funded by repeated dilutive equity offerings — share count has roughly doubled over the past year, and further capital raises are likely as the fleet scales

29% short interest cuts both ways — a beat can trigger a violent short squeeze (Q4 2025: ~+11% pre-market, another ~+10% intraday), but a miss or a fresh dilutive-offering announcement can trigger an equally sharp reversal (-19.5% over 10 days in late July 2026)
Unit economics of robot delivery at scale remain genuinely unproven — losses widened 159% YoY in FY2025 even as revenue grew
